name: Transdermal oxybutynin dose-ranging trial
question: Does transdermal oxybutynin reduce urge or mixed urinary incontinence compared with placebo in adults with overactive bladder?

design.population: Adults at least 18 years old with overactive bladder and at least 10 urge incontinence episodes and 56 voids in a baseline 7-day diary, with pure urge or urge-predominant mixed incontinence, after symptom stabilization or treatment withdrawal.
design.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, Study population and Table 1, pp 581-582

verdictNote: Dunnett-adjusted rank ANCOVA for the 3.9-mg/day dose was significant (P=0.0165).
takeaway: Among 520 randomized adults with urge or urge-predominant mixed incontinence (512 modified intention-to-treat), transdermal oxybutynin 3.9 mg/day improved median weekly leakage versus placebo at 12 weeks (−19.0 versus −14.5; Dunnett-adjusted rank ANCOVA P=0.0165).

reports.label: Dose-ranging randomized report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed citation and Crossref publication month: August 2002; day approximated
reports.citation: Dmochowski RR, Davila GW, Zinner NR, et al. "Efficacy and safety of transdermal oxybutynin in patients with urge and mixed urinary incontinence." *J Urol.* 2002;168(2):580-586. doi:10.1016/S0022-5347(05)64684-8
reports.followUp: 12 weeks blinded, followed by 12 weeks open-label dose titration
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 581

results.measure: Median change in weekly incontinence episodes at 12 weeks
results.note: The 3.9-mg/day contrast was significant by Dunnett-adjusted rank ANCOVA (P=0.0165); the 0.016 Bonferroni per-dose value was used for sample-size estimation. The FDA statistical review reported parametric ANCOVA P=0.2831 and post-audit site-exclusion reanalysis P=0.0265. Modified intention-to-treat analysis used last observation carried forward.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical methodology, p 582; Results and Table 2, pp 582-583

results.measure: Mean change in daily voiding frequency at 12 weeks
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 582; Figure 3, p 583

results.measure: Median change in average voided volume at 12 weeks, 3.9 mg/day versus placebo
results.note: The reported difference was significant only at baseline-volume values in the first and second quartiles, including the median; it was not significant above the baseline median of 167 mL.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 582; Figure 4, p 583

results.measure: Median change in average voided volume at 12 weeks, 2.6 mg/day versus placebo
results.note: The reported difference was significant only at baseline-volume values in the first and second quartiles, including the median; it was not significant above the baseline median of 167 mL.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 582; Figure 4, p 583

results.measure: Incontinence Impact Questionnaire total score at 12 weeks

values.exp: 39% improvement in mean total score (modified intention-to-treat n=123)
values.ctl: 28% improvement in mean total score (modified intention-to-treat n=130)

results.note: Mean IIQ total score improved by 39% with 3.9 mg/day versus 28% with placebo.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 582; Figure 5, p 584

results.measure: No incontinence episodes in the diary at 12-week endpoint
results.note: Descriptive counts; no between-group comparison reported.
results.locator: Full text, Outcome measures, p 581; Results and Table 2, pp 582-583

harms.locator: Full text, Safety, p 584; Table 1, p 582
harms.note: Treatment-related application-site pruritus during double-blind treatment.

harms.label: Dry mouth
harms.locator: Full text, Table 3 and Safety, p 584
harms.note: Combined active-dose incidence 27/388 (7.0%) versus 11/132 (8.3%) with placebo; P=0.98.

harms.label: Application-site erythema
harms.locator: Full text, Safety, p 584; Table 1, p 582

harms.label: Treatment discontinuation for adverse events
harms.note: 53/520 (10.2%) discontinued during double-blind treatment because of adverse events; 25 withdrew for application-site reactions. In the open-label period, Safety reports 30/411 (7.3%) adverse-event discontinuations and 15 application-site-reaction withdrawals; the Results withdrawal summary instead reports 33 open-label adverse-event withdrawals.

delivery.label: Patch application and extension
delivery.value: Two systems combining active and matching placebo 13-cm² and 26-cm² patches were applied to the abdomen twice weekly to deliver 1.3, 2.6, or 3.9 mg/day during 12 blinded weeks. In the 12-week open-label extension, all began at 1.3 mg/day, with titration to 2.6 or 3.9 mg/day after weeks 2 and 4 according to symptoms and adverse effects.
delivery.locator: Full text, Study drug treatment and procedures, p 581

delivery.label: Treatment completion and final extension dose
delivery.value: 447/520 (86.0%) completed double-blind treatment; 411 entered and 358/411 (87.1%) completed the open-label extension. Final extension doses were 3.9 mg/day for 211/411 (51.3%), 2.6 mg/day for 139/411 (33.8%), and 1.3 mg/day for 61/411 (14.8%).

delivery.label: Patch adherence and dosing compliance
delivery.value: Dosing compliance was approximately 90% throughout the study; more than 90% patch adherence was observed at more than 90% of application-site evaluations.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, p 582; application-site evaluation, p 584
